\begin{definition}[Growth exponent]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gev}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gev}
\leanok
For natural numbers $E$, $\ell$, and $s$, define the growth exponent
$g(E,\ell,s)=2E\ell+2Es$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exponentiation by gev]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gKv}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gKv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gev}
For natural numbers $E$, $\ell_g$, and $s$, define
$gKv(E,\ell_g,s)=2^{\operatorname{gev}(E,\ell_g,s)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Input-length scan initialization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gscan_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gscan_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $\mathcal O$ be
an oracle with four query types on finite Boolean words. Suppose that for every $k\le
|x|$, query type $0$ on the encoding of $x$ together with the binary word for $k$
returns true exactly when $k<|x|$. Let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a
register state whose registers are all at most $B$, with $\sigma.n\le |x|$ and $|x|\le
B$. If the procedure started in state $lg0$ with $n=|x|$ and all other registers as in
$\sigma$ terminates on every sequence of choices while keeping every register at most
$B$, and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the same semantic property holds from
state $scan$ with registers $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halving-stage initialization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.ghalf_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.ghalf_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.size_half, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.half, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jz_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jz_pos}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four
query types and each finite Boolean word, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $Q$
be a proposition. Let $\sigma$ be a register state in which every register is at most
$B$, and suppose $\sigma.lg+\operatorname{size}(\sigma.n)\le B$. If the procedure,
started in the round state with false phase and index $E$, with $n=0$ and
$lg=\sigma.lg+\operatorname{size}(\sigma.n)$ and all other registers as in $\sigma$,
terminates on every sequence of choices while keeping every register at most $B$, and
accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the same termination, register-bound, and
acceptance property holds when started in the halving-test state with registers
$\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Grounding a counting round]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.grounds_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.grounds_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_e, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_k, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rY, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.re, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rk, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.toV_rY, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_addTwice}
\difficulty{5}
Fix natural numbers $E,B$, an oracle $\mathcal O:[4]\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$, a
Boolean word $x$, a proposition $Q$, and a phase
$ph\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For every $j\in\mathbb N$ with $j<E+1$ and
every counting state $\sigma$ whose register values are all at most $B$, suppose
$\sigma.e+2j(if\ ph\ then\sigma.s\ else\sigma.lg)\le B$. If, for every $k'\le B$, the
counting procedure started in round state $0$ with phase $ph$, with $e$ increased by
$2j(if\ ph\ then\sigma.s\ else\sigma.lg)$ and $k=k'$, terminates on every sequence of
choices while keeping every register at most $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds,
then the procedure started in round state $j$ with phase $ph$ and registers $\sigma$ has
that same termination, register-bound, and acceptance property.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Doubling the code bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gdouble_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gdouble_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rK, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rT, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rk, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jz_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jz_pos, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_addTwice, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_dec}
\difficulty{5}
Fix $E,B\in\mathbb N$, an oracle on four indices and Boolean strings, an input bit
string $x$, a proposition $Q$, and a register state $\sigma$. For every $m\in\mathbb N$
such that $\sigma.e=m$, suppose all seventeen quantities in $\sigma$ are at most $B$,
$\sigma.K\,2^m\le B$, and for every $k',T'\le B$ the procedure started in state
$\mathrm{st0}$ with $e=0$, $K=\sigma.K\,2^m$, $k=k'$, and $T=T'$ terminates with all
registers at most $B$ and accepts if and only if $Q$ holds. Then the procedure started
in state $\mathrm{db}$ with state $\sigma$ terminates with all registers at most $B$ and
accepts if and only if $Q$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Iterated Ball Nonacceptance]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.iter_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.iter_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.RelO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Clear, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.ball, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rK, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rk, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gKv, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gdouble_run, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gev, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.grdX, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.grounds_run, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gstage, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be an
oracle, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a state
of the counting procedure. Set $K=2^{2E\sigma.lg+2E\sigma.s}$, and form the balls using
the relation and initial predicate determined by $\mathrm{orc}$, $x$, and $\sigma.s$.
Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, its exponent register is zero, its
designated scratch registers are clear, $K+1\le B$, and the ball of radius zero has
cardinality one. Suppose that for every $k',T',v',c'\le B$, the counting procedure at
its comparison stage, with exponent zero, code bound and stage index $K$, next stage
index $K+1$, those four register values, and the ball of radius $K$'s cardinality in its
known-ball-size register, terminates and has accepting computation exactly when $Q$
holds. Then the procedure started at $\sigma$ in the false-phase round state with $E$
rounds remaining terminates, and has an accepting computation exactly when both $Q$
holds and no vertex in any ball of radius $j$, for $0<j\le K$, is accepting.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison stage semantics]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.cmp_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.cmp_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rcp, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rn, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.ret, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $E,B\in\mathbb N$, an oracle
$\mathrm{orc}:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, an input
bit string $x$, a proposition $Q$, and a register state $\sigma$ consisting of the
seventeen natural-number quantities specified for the counting procedure. Suppose each
quantity in $\sigma$ is at most $B$ and $\sigma.s+1\le B$. If $\sigma.cp\ne\sigma.n$,
assume the procedure started in round state $\mathrm{rd}(\mathrm{false},E)$ with $n$
replaced by $\sigma.cp$ and $s$ replaced by $\sigma.s+1$ terminates with all registers
at most $B$, and accepts if and only if $Q$ holds. Then, started in comparison state
$\mathrm{cmp}$ with state $\sigma$, it terminates with all registers at most $B$ and
accepts if and only if $\sigma.cp=\sigma.n$ or both $\sigma.cp\ne\sigma.n$ and $Q$ hold.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initialization of the Counting Run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.start_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.start_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.lgv, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.lt_two_pow_size_succ, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.ghalf_run, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gscan_run, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $\mathcal{O}$ assign a
Boolean answer to each of four query types and each bit string, and let $Q$ be a
proposition. Suppose that for every $k\le |x|$, the answer to query type $0$ on the
encoding of $x$ with the binary representation of $k$ is true exactly when $k<|x|$.
Suppose also that $2^{\operatorname{size}(|x|)+1}\le B$. If, from the initial round
state with the logarithm register set to $\operatorname{size}(|x|)+1$ and all other
registers zero, every sequence of choices terminates while every register stays at most
$B$, and the machine accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the same properties hold from
the initial scan state with all registers zero.
\end{theorem}
